clue.text: Amount of pressure girl talked of at pub

indicators.note: talked of says the girl's name is only to be heard spoken, giving a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: Millie is a girl's name
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone describes the pressure a young woman is under at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talked of' turns MILLIE into the sound MILLI, which is then followed by BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A millibar is a unit of atmospheric pressure, a thousandth of a bar, used in weather forecasts.

clue.text: He painted industrial buildings extending over road

indicators.note: extending over says the buildings stretch around the road

parts.note: mills are factories
AI stands for the A1, Britain's Great North Road, written with an I in crosswords

explanation.surface: An artist depicted factories spreading across a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extending over' has the factories stretch round the road. Road numbers like A1 are written AI in crosswords. John Everett Millais was a Victorian Pre-Raphaelite painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Millais was a famous English painter, so he is someone who painted.

clue.text: Fate of one whose wife should be remembered

definitions.text: one whose wife should be remembered

explanation.surface: The destiny of a man whose wife must never be forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remember Lot's wife' is a Bible verse (Luke 17:32); she was turned into a pillar of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's fate; the other sense is the Old Testament figure whose wife looked back.

clue.text: Terrible poison present in this gaseous envelope?

indicators.note: terrible says the letters of poison are in a bad way and scrambled

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A dreadful toxin is lurking in the air surrounding us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like it describes the poison but signals the rearrangement (IONOSP). The question mark admits the ionosphere is only one layer of the gaseous envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The ionosphere is the layer of ionised gas in Earth's upper atmosphere, part of the planet's gaseous envelope.

clue.text: Useful quality bishop missed in hunting dog

indicators.note: missed means the bishop is left out of the dog's name

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hunting hound
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman fails to turn up for a hunt with hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: BASSET without B gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable feature or advantage, so a useful quality.

clue.text: Chairperson's appeal bringing favourable return

parts.note: a professor holds a university chair, so the chairperson is a prof
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A committee chair makes a plea that brings in a good result.
explanation.definitionFit: A profit is a gain on money laid out, so it is a return that favours the investor.

clue.text: Not common like Ben Jonson!

explanation.surface: The playwright Ben Jonson was out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson's tomb in Westminster Abbey bears the epitaph 'O rare Ben Jonson'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon; the other sense is the famous epitaph praising the playwright.

clue.text: A flag, possibly, might identify this hippy cult

definitions.text: A flag, possibly, might identify this hippy cult

parts.words: A flag, possibly, might identify this hippy cult
parts.note: a flag is also an iris, so it is a bloom, and naming one shows the force of blooms, the 1960s hippy slogan

explanation.surface: A banner carried by protesters could mark out a sixties counterculture movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the iris plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Flower power was the 1960s hippy movement promoting peace and love, symbolised by flowers.

clue.text: Attempt to embrace woman where hides are treated

indicators.note: to embrace says the attempt wraps its arms round the woman

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man tries to hug a woman in the place where she is hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' looks like a verb for concealing; it means animal skins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where animal skins are tanned into leather.

clue.text: Reveller's vehicle right at bottom of river

indicators.note: at bottom of places the right below the river in this down entry

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A partygoer's car has ended up at the bottom of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes the 's, read as 'is': a reveller is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who drinks and makes merry noisily, a reveller.

clue.text: Make whoopee, lowering the shock level

explanation.surface: Partying hard is described as letting a jolt drop to a lower setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'shock' as a shock of hair: letting it fall lowers its level.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax and enjoy oneself without inhibition is the idiom's sense, which matches having a wild time.

clue.text: Grammatical relationship in patois developed around Italian valley

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters are wrapped about the valley
developed means these letters have been worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, part of the material to be rearranged
the Po valley is the great river plain of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A linguist notes a grammatical feature in the local dialect of a north Italian valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the material that 'developed' rearranges (into APSITION); 'around' then wraps it round the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposition is the grammatical relation of two noun phrases side by side naming the same thing, as in 'my brother, the doctor'.

clue.text: Aggravating expert going over case

indicators.note: going over places the expert on top of the case in this down entry

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
the vocative is the grammatical case used for addressing someone

explanation.surface: A specialist reviewing a file is being irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is not a file but a grammatical case; 'going over' puts PRO above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Provocative behaviour deliberately annoys or stirs up anger, which is aggravating.

clue.text: Surrender, taking 31 days over conclusion of truce

indicators.note: over signals that the month's short form is turned back to front

parts.note: December has 31 days, abbreviated Dec

indicators.note: conclusion of picks the final letter of the word truce

explanation.surface: Someone gives in, having taken a month to bring a ceasefire to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the month round (CED). '31 days' could be several months; only December fits the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to yield or give up territory or rights, the same as surrendering them.

clue.text: Lacking marches, unlike the Edinburgh Festival?

explanation.surface: Without border territories, the Scottish arts festival would be quite different.
explanation.walkthrough: Marches are border regions, i.e. fringes; the Edinburgh Festival is famous for its Fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: Marches and fringes are both edges, so being without them is having no fringe; the festival has one.

clue.text: Conceal spades beside dam

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: Someone hides a spade next to a barrier across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' is not the river barrier but a female parent of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it up so thoroughly that it is hidden or suppressed.

clue.text: Speaker loses head, securing help over heating device

indicators.note: securing means the beheaded speaker holds the help firmly inside
loses head means the speaker's first letter is dropped

parts.note: an orator is a speaker

indicators.note: over turns the word for help upside down in this down entry

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A speechmaker is decapitated while getting assistance with the central heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' leaves RATOR and 'over' turns the help upwards (DIA), which 'securing' holds inside. 'Speaker' looks like a loudspeaker, a device like the answer, but it is a person making speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiator is a device that heats a room by passing hot water through metal panels.

clue.text: Bolshie left back stabbing agent

indicators.note: stabbing means one piece is thrust into the middle of the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: back signals that the word for left is read in reverse

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A football defender on the left knifes an undercover operative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left back' reads like a football position; in fact 'back' turns the port side round (TROP), and 'stabbing' drives it in. 'Bolshie' is British slang for awkward and rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy and bolshie are both British informal words for bad-tempered and uncooperative.

clue.text: Searched southern state accompanied by Times boss

indicators.note: accompanied by places the second piece right after the first

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for South Carolina, a southern US state
from the newspaper's own point of view, its boss is our editor, OUR ED

explanation.surface: A southern US state is searched with the help of the newspaper's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears in The Times, so its own editor is 'our ED'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour an area is to search it thoroughly, so scoured is a past-tense synonym for searched.

clue.text: Breathing aid man's set up on boat out East

indicators.note: set up means the word is written upwards, reversed in this down entry

parts.note: Ron's is a man's name with the possessive

indicators.note: out says East is removed from the boat word

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A man's diving gear is set up on a boat heading out east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns RONS into SNOR; KEEL without E gives KEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel is a tube that lets a swimmer breathe with their face underwater.

clue.text: One reviving sheep, replacing old one in French painting?

indicators.note: replacing says the sheep is put in place of the old one in the painting

parts.note: a Renoir is a painting by the French Impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir
O is short for old, and I is the Roman numeral one
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Someone restores a French Impressionist canvas by putting a sheep in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping EWE for the O and I of RENOIR gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who renews something brings it back to freshness, so a renewer revives things.

clue.text: Attack ends of laboratory entering quietly and at speed

indicators.note: entering marks one piece going into the other; here the quiet letter goes in

parts.note: a raid is an attack
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: ends of picks the first and last letters of laboratory

explanation.surface: A raid on the lab ends with the attackers slipping in silently and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' sits oddly: the quiet letter enters the attack-plus-lab-ends, after its first two letters, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly means quickly, so it is done at speed.

clue.text: Examination of literary work disregarding past

indicators.note: disregarding means the word for time gone by is left out

parts.note: a pastoral is a literary work idealising country life
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar studies a book while ignoring its history.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove PAST from PASTORAL to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a viva or language test.

clue.text: Daughter leaves in a fluster, reversing some old banger

indicators.note: leaves says the daughter departs from the flustered word

parts.note: rattled means flustered

indicators.note: reversing turns the word for some back to front

parts.note: part means some

explanation.surface: A flustered daughter drives off, backing up an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: RATTLED loses D to give RATTLE; 'reversing' makes TRAP of PART. A banger is British slang for a dilapidated old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a rickety, noisy old vehicle, just what an old banger is.

clue.text: Right contents of barn left for husband?

indicators.note: for says the left is swapped in where the husband stood

parts.note: a tithe barn held the tithes, a tenth of produce paid to the church

explanation.surface: A farm's grain is all that remains as of right after the husband walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: In TITHE, L replaces H.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a legal right to ownership of property.

clue.text: In Ecuador he acknowledged a S American runner

indicators.note: In says the answer lies inside the run of words Ecuador he acknowledged

explanation.surface: In South America, a man thanked someone for running.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Ecuador', 'he' and the start of 'acknowledged'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless bird of South America that runs fast, like an ostrich.

clue.text: Trucker who held other travellers up?

explanation.surface: A lorry driver is accused of having robbed people on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a highwayman, who held up coaches; 'held up' means robbed, not delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was once a jocular name for a highwayman and is now used for a long-distance lorry driver.

clue.text: Of limited desirability at first, like one's school tie?

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An old school tie is not very appealing at first glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old school tie' stands for privileged networks of former pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: An old school tie is one worn by former pupils, so it is described by the adjective.

clue.text: General procedure for producing play

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way of doing something is a procedure

explanation.surface: A military commander's method for staging a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is not a drama but slack, as in play in a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to move or freedom of action, the same as play in a mechanism.

clue.text: Attorney in safety organisation finds time to celebrate

indicators.note: in puts the attorney inside the word safety before the rearranging
